title: From Worship, Now, Thy Church Dismiss
description: From Worship, Now, Thy Church Dismiss in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Hosea Ballou wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 88 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Dismission”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From wor-ship, now, thy church dis-miss But not with-out thy bless-ing, Lord; O grant a taste of heav-enly bliss, And seal in-struc-tion from thy word.

lines: From worship, now, thy church dismiss —
But not without thy blessing, Lord;
O grant a taste of heavenly bliss,
And seal instruction from thy word.
Oft may these pleasant scenes return
When we shall meet to worship thee;
Oft may our hearts within us burn
To hear thy word, thy goodness see.
And when these pleasant scenes are past,
To thee, our God, O may we come,
And meet th' assembled world at last,

licence: Public domain: Hosea Ballou died in 1852.
credits: Words by Hosea Ballou (1771–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
